A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAA/AFP distillation framework, renamed from FOFA to PAT. All supplied pages, equations, figures, and tables support comparison. Neither PDF contains an appendix or the separately referenced implementation supplement.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and object-detection results, component and hyperparameter ablations, and attention visualizations in Tables 1–6 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a KL-loss ablation and training-complexity measurements in Tables 7–8.

M1.justification: FOFA is renamed PAT, but RAA, AFP, previous-iteration feedback, teacher regularization, and the combined training objective remain unchanged. Removing KL supervision is confined to a new ablation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-100 and ImageNet classification and COCO object detection. The new analyses use existing CIFAR-100 teacher–student pairs without introducing another dataset, task, domain, or test scenario.

E2.justification: Classification retains KD, DKD, DIST, OFA, FitNet, CC, RKD, and CRD; detection retains KD, DKD, OFA, and FitNet. The new ablation and complexity tables reuse existing comparison methods.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged. Sections 5.4–5.5 introduce a control omitting the logits KL loss on three CIFAR-100 model pairs and evaluate extra parameter counts and seconds per epoch for ConvNeXt-T–DeiT-T.

E4.justification: Tables 7–8 substantially extend the diagnostic analysis by testing dependence on logits supervision and comparing training complexity against other methods. These address attribution of the gains and computational cost beyond the retained module, AFP-placement, query-count, and attention-map analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions state that their results are averaged over three trials. Neither supplies seeds, standard deviations, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and v2 introduces no different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–6 are unchanged. New Table 7 reports no-KL accuracies of 79.14, 75.98, and 81.79; Table 8 adds parameter and timing results. Table 7 also lists 79.10 for full PAT on ConvNeXt-T–DeiT-T, conflicting with the retained 79.59 in Table 1 without explaining a setting difference.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain the same mathematical content apart from renaming the framework. The expanded loss description clarifies existing quantities; neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about resolving view mismatch and teacher unawareness through RAA and AFP. The claimed classification and detection gains are unchanged despite the new title and framework name.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 newly discusses whether gains depend on logits matching and interprets performance without KL supervision. Section 5.5 acknowledges higher training cost, states that extra parameters introduce no student inference overhead, and discusses reducing AFP modules or queries to trade performance for efficiency.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and reports extra parameter counts and epoch times in Table 8. These improve access information and resource disclosure, although hardware and detailed training instructions remain unavailable in the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hamidi et al. (2024) on teacher training for effective distillation and Wang et al. (2024) on feature norm and direction regularization. Section 2.3 adds a comparison with retraining teachers using MSE, while the principal positioning against OFA and prior prompt-based methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title and framework name, revises author information, introduces numbered headings and acknowledgments, and edits several explanatory paragraphs. Most prose and the overall progression from motivation through methods, experiments, and conclusion remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 7–8, rearranges existing displays, and changes typography and reference formatting. Figure 1 distinguishes brown dashed connections, Figure 2 updates notation, and classification tables drop venue/year subheaders. Existing result displays and attention maps are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the new KL-loss ablation and complexity comparison provide useful evidence about the source of the gains and training overhead, while the code link improves access information. The improvement is limited: the principal results remain unchanged, detailed implementation information is still absent, and Table 7 introduces an unexplained 79.10 versus 79.59 discrepancy.
